title: Reframing the dental hygiene workforce crisis
html: Access to oral health care in the United States is increasingly constrained not by the number of dentists but by the availability and use of the broader dental team. Among them, dental hygienists play a central role in the prevention and maintenance of various oral conditions, yet workforce challenges have emerged as a critical barrier to timely patient care.1,2 Data from Maine provide a useful lens through which to examine the deeper structural challenges in workforce distribution, retention, and delivery.
